title: Honest evidence, calm answers and clear meeting reports
course_title: Presentation Skills: Talks, Pitches and Community Meetings

say: Honest evidence, calm answers, and clear meeting reports.
This is the video for module three of Presentation Skills.
People are persuaded by facts and feelings. A number shows something is real. A story makes people care.

panel.heading: A talk is only as strong as trust
items: Facts show it is real; stories make people care
Never claim more than you can prove

say: But one exaggerated figure that someone later checks can damage your name more than a weak talk ever would.

say: And community meetings are where many real decisions are made. Speaking well there can win support for a project.

say: For example, Zainab leads a women's group in Kaduna that trains young mothers in hairdressing. She is pitching to a foundation. From her register, 36 trainees started and 29 finished. That is roughly 8 in 10.

panel.heading: Zainab's honest numbers
items: Admit the limit: incomes not recorded

say: Follow-up calls showed 17 of the 29 graduates now earn from hairdressing. She says exactly that, not most of our women are now successful.

panel.heading: Zainab's honest numbers
items: Admit the limit: incomes not recorded

say: She adds one story, with permission, about a graduate who now runs a small salon corner. A good story is short and true: situation, problem, action, result.

panel.heading: Zainab's honest numbers
items: Admit the limit: incomes not recorded

say: Incomes were not recorded, so she makes no claim about earnings. Never round 12 customers up to dozens, and never say NAFDAC approved unless you hold the number.

panel.heading: Zainab's honest numbers
items: Admit the limit: incomes not recorded
panel.rule: Check every claim against a record. Drop what you cannot prove.

say: Before the day, write down the ten questions you would least like to be asked, and prepare a short answer to each. Then use four steps.

panel.heading: Listen, pause, answer, check
items: Pause, and restate it for the room
Check: does that answer your question?

say: Listen to the whole question without interrupting.

panel.heading: Listen, pause, answer, check
items: Pause, and restate it for the room
Check: does that answer your question?

say: Pause for a second or two. In a large room, restate the question so everyone hears it.

panel.heading: Listen, pause, answer, check
items: Pause, and restate it for the room
Check: does that answer your question?

say: Answer briefly. The direct answer first, then one reason or example. Nervous speakers often give a five-minute speech and lose the room.

panel.heading: Listen, pause, answer, check
items: Pause, and restate it for the room
Check: does that answer your question?

say: Then check, does that answer your question, and move on. If you do not know, say so: I will send it to you by Friday.

panel.heading: Listen, pause, answer, check
items: Pause, and restate it for the room
Check: does that answer your question?
panel.rule: Not sure? Say "I don't know", and follow up by a set date.

say: For example, Mercy presents yearly accounts to 50 members in Calabar. A man stands and shouts: last year money went missing. Why should we trust these numbers?

panel.heading: Mercy and the angry member
items: Answers with facts in under a minute

say: Mercy listens fully, without interrupting.

panel.heading: Mercy and the angry member
items: Answers with facts in under a minute

say: She restates: the question is whether these accounts can be trusted after last year's problem.

panel.heading: Mercy and the angry member
items: Answers with facts in under a minute

say: In under a minute she explains: two signatories are now needed for every withdrawal, the bank statements are on the table, and two members checked the books.

panel.heading: Mercy and the angry member
items: Answers with facts in under a minute

say: She checks, invites him to see the statements at the break, and moves on.

panel.heading: Mercy and the angry member
items: Answers with facts in under a minute
panel.rule: Stay calm, name the real concern, point to evidence.

say: Get the agenda, greet the chair and elders briefly according to custom, and speak through the chair: Madam Chair. Then report in a fixed order.

panel.heading: A report in five parts
items: Close: repeat the decision, invite questions

say: First, your purpose and main message.

panel.heading: A report in five parts
items: Close: repeat the decision, invite questions

say: What was done since the last meeting. Pass round photos rather than describing at length.

panel.heading: A report in five parts
items: Close: repeat the decision, invite questions

say: The money, in its simplest form.

panel.heading: A report in five parts
items: Close: repeat the decision, invite questions

say: Next steps, and the decision you need.

panel.heading: A report in five parts
items: Close: repeat the decision, invite questions

say: Then close by repeating the decision, and invite questions through the chair.

panel.heading: A report in five parts
items: Close: repeat the decision, invite questions

say: Here is a money report members can check. These figures are illustrative.
Grace starts with the opening balance: 150,000 naira.
Contributions received: 450,000 naira.
Spent: 520,000 naira, on 120 metres of drain cleared and repaired.
So the closing balance is 80,000 naira. She checks the sum before the meeting, and says where receipts and bank statements can be inspected.
A motion is a clear proposal people can vote on. Grace says: I move that we approve a 5,000 naira levy for phase two.

panel.heading: End with a motion, keep it safe
items: Say what, how much, who and by when
Never post members' payments in the group
If threatened: ask the chair, keep an exit

say: It says what, how much, who and by when: due by the end of next month, from 80 households, giving 400,000 naira.

panel.heading: End with a motion, keep it safe
items: Say what, how much, who and by when
Never post members' payments in the group
If threatened: ask the chair, keep an exit

say: Afterwards, share a short summary on the WhatsApp group, but never post individual members' payment status there without agreement.

panel.heading: End with a motion, keep it safe
items: Say what, how much, who and by when
Never post members' payments in the group
If threatened: ask the chair, keep an exit

say: If anyone becomes threatening, do not argue back or move closer. Ask the chair to manage the meeting, keep a clear path to the exit, and leave if you feel unsafe.

panel.heading: End with a motion, keep it safe
items: Say what, how much, who and by when
Never post members' payments in the group
If threatened: ask the chair, keep an exit
panel.rule: If a meeting turns threatening, your safety comes first.

say: To remember. Use a few sourced numbers and one true story. Never claim what you cannot prove. Listen, pause, answer, check. Report in five parts. And make sure the money adds up.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Two or three sourced numbers, plus one true story
Never claim what you cannot prove
Report: purpose, actions, money, decision, close
Money must add up and be open to check

say: Now check every claim in your talk, practise your ten hardest questions with a friend, and draft a 5-minute meeting report with a motion.
